It can be daunting to talk about money with a partner, but there's a reason they say that being on the same page about your finances is like relationship gold. So we asked relationship experts what the biggest issues that come up are and what you can do about them. First, there's the big one, which is really common. People argue about money because it means very different things to each of us. Most of us learned about money from our parents, either directly or indirectly. So if your partner grew up in a household where money was a source of stress and anxiety, they may feel like money is something to be managed or hoarded. If your parents treated money casually, you might not worry about it as much. A lack of communication is another common trap. You may not feel comfortable talking about money because it's embarrassing to you, or because you never saw it as a thing to talk about. It can be a scary thing, like wondering if your partner would be okay if you suddenly lost your income. Money is a reflection of power, too. It's natural to defer to the partner who makes more money in a relationship, but over time, that may lead to the other partner feeling like they've lost their voice. Here's where it helps to be honest about what you want your life together to look like. This is a way to look past all the history you might carry about money and to find a future together that fits both of you. And a lot of experts suggest starting that conversation right now.
